headline: 6 EVM contracts catalogued across Ethereum, BSC, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon; Asgard vault addresses dynamic (TSS-churned); native THORChain chain and UTXO chains use non-EVM TSS vault addresses not suitable for static registry.

Router 0xD37BbE5744D730a1d98d8DC97c42F0Ca46aD7146 confirmed via Blockscan multichain data on ETH, BSC, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, and Polygon. Non-EVM chains (Bitcoin, Dogecoin, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Ripple, Cosmos, Solana, Tron) use dynamic Asgard TSS vault addresses that churn regularly; zero static addresses surfaced for these chains — see unknowns.

THORChain Router has no factory/pool enumeration methods (ABI confirmed: deposit, depositWithExpiry, transferOut, transferOutAndCall, returnVaultAssets, transferAllowance, vaultAllowance). Asgard vault addresses are ephemeral TSS multi-party addresses managed by the THORNode network, not child contracts of a factory. Cap notice: vault enumeration not applicable to this architecture.

Role taxonomy applied: Router (router), Deployer EOA (admin/other), Old RUNE Token (token). Asgard vaults classified as 'vault' but dynamic. A second router variant 0xdEC999d968369Ce6C88E41C140F17a2Ce54e9Cb0 observed in deployer transaction history — role unverified this run.

All admin_addresses entries trace to fetched Etherscan URLs. The router variant 0xdEC999d968369Ce6C88E41C140F17a2Ce54e9Cb0 was observed only in deployer transaction records (snippet-level sighting) — placed in unknowns, not admin_addresses, pending verification.

protocol_metadata.about: THORChain is a Cosmos SDK-based Layer 1 decentralized exchange that enables native cross-chain swaps without wrapped tokens or bridges. Users swap assets (e.g., BTC for ETH) by sending to dynamic Asgard vault addresses on external chains; THORChain nodes observe inbounds and release outbounds using GG20 Threshold Signature Scheme (TSS). Liquidity is managed via continuous liquidity pools (CLPs) on the THORChain native chain, with RUNE as the settlement asset paired in every pool. EVM chains (Ethereum, BSC, Avalanche, Base) use an immutable Router contract that handles token deposits and outbound transfers via memo-embedded transactions; native asset chains (Bitcoin, Dogecoin, etc.) interact directly with churning TSS vault addresses.
